content: Permethrin is a medication that eliminates parasites and their eggs. It is specifically used to treat scabies, a skin infestation, as well as lice infestations affecting the head, body, and pubic area (commonly referred to as crabs). However, it is important to note that permethrin does not prevent these infestations from occurring. Permethrin is available in two forms: a cream and a liquid (cream rinse), both intended for external use only. Typically, a single application is sufficient to eradicate the parasites. However, if signs of infestation, such as live parasites, reappear, the treatment may need to be repeated after one week. In such cases, you should contact your doctor. Always follow the instructions provided on the package or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use permethrin exactly as directed, and do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. If you have open cuts or scratches on your hands, wear rubber gloves when applying the medication. If permethrin accidentally comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water for at least five minutes. If you are using the liquid form of permethrin, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hair with your regular shampoo. 2. Rinse your hair thoroughly and towel-dry your hair and scalp. 3. Allow your hair to air dry for a few minutes. 4. Do not stand or sit in a shower or bathtub while applying the liquid. Instead, lean over a sink. 5. Shake the bottle of liquid well before use. 6. Thoroughly wet your hair and scalp with the liquid, ensuring you cover the areas behind your ears and the back of your neck. 7. Leave the liquid on your hair for 10 minutes before rinsing it off thoroughly with water. 8. Dry your hair with a clean towel. 9. Use a fine-tooth comb to remove nits (lice eggs and larvae). 10. Wash your hands thoroughly to remove any residual medication. If you are using the cream form of permethrin, follow these steps: 1. Wash your entire body or take a shower. 2. Massage the cream thoroughly into your skin, covering your entire body from head to toe. 3. Leave the cream on your skin for 8 to 14 hours. 4. After 8 to 14 hours, wash the cream off by taking another shower. If you have head lice, wash combs and brushes with permethrin liquid and rinse them thoroughly with water to remove the medication. Before using permethrin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to permethrin or any other medications. Additionally, let them know about any prescription or nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Pregnant individuals should wear gloves when applying permethrin to another person to prevent absorption through the skin. Permethrin may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Skin irritation Rash Redness Swelling Store permethrin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Permethrin is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. After using permethrin, machine-wash or dry-clean all clothing, bed linens, and towels used in the past two days. Use hot water and dry them in a hot dryer for at least 20 minutes. Thoroughly clean all bathtubs, showers, and toilets in your home with rubbing alcohol. If you have scabies, it is possible that you may have transmitted the parasites to family members or close contacts, including sexual partners. Advise them to see a doctor if they develop symptoms of infestation. Itching may persist for several weeks after treatment if your skin has become sensitive to the parasites. This does not necessarily indicate treatment failure. Contact your doctor if you have any concerns or questions. Do not share your medication with others. If you have any questions about permethrin, consult your pharmacist.
